title: Automatic rollback controller for inference-config changes: triggers, guardrails, and state reconciliation
creator: Ava Patel
description: Implement an automated rollback controller for configuration changes that affect batching and caching behaviors. The controller should detect unsafe or costly regressions introduced by automated recommendations or manual config applies, enforce guardrails to prevent unsafe rollouts, and reconcile desired vs actual state so drift or partial failures don't leave clusters in an inconsistent configuration. This specifically covers: recommended batching/caching profile application, autoscaling config changes, and runtime kernel/quantization profile flips that can materially affect latency, error rate, or cost per token.
acceptance_criteria:
- Controller triggers a rollback automatically when one or more configured safety conditions breach for a sustained window (e.g., p99 latency increase > 40% for 5 minutes, error rate > 0.5% for 3 minutes, cost per token > 30% above baseline for 10 minutes).
- Rollbacks are safe and idempotent: after rollback the observed metrics must return to within 10% of baseline within 15 minutes, or an operator will be paged.
- All config changes (automated recommendations and manual applies) are audited with before/after snapshots and an event with a rollback reason.
- System performs state reconciliation every 1 minute and corrects drift without duplicating change events.
- Canary/staged applies supported: 1%, 5%, 25% cohorts with automatic expansion or immediate rollback on canary failure.
- End-to-end integration tests covering canary fail, global rollback, and reconciliation pass in CI.
- Documentation and runbook for operators completed and reviewed by SRE and product teams.
implementation_plan: 1) Design a lightweight rollback controller process that subscribes to config-change events (recommendation apply, manual API call, UI apply). 2) Define a pluggable trigger system: threshold triggers (latency/error/cost), statistical regressions (KS test or bootstrap on request latency), and external signals (customer SLA alert). 3) Implement guardrails: minimum healthy capacity, cooldown windows, max rollback frequency, and canary cohort logic. 4) Build a reconciliation loop that snapshots desired config (Control Plane), queries runtime nodes for actual config, calculates diffs, and issues idempotent apply/rollback ops. 5) Integrate telemetry: baseline calculation service, anomaly detector, and alerting rules. 6) Add RBAC and audit metadata to every action. 7) Add comprehensive unit/integration tests and staging rollout. 8) Docs + runbook + pager routing.
triggers_and_guardrails:
Triggers to wire up:
- Latency SLO breach: p99 > baseline * 1.4 for 5m
- Error spike: 3x baseline error rate or absolute > 0.5% for 3m
- Cost spike: cost per token increases > 30% over rolling 10m window
- Throughput regression: sustained throughput drop > 20% for 5m impacting capacity SLAs
- Model fallback events (incompatible kernel/runtime failure)
Guardrails: 
- Minimum healthy capacity threshold prevents applying changes that would reduce pool below X GPUs or X routes.
- Canary timeouts: if canary doesn't reach steady-state metrics in Y minutes, automatically rollback.
- Max-rollback-rate: no more than N automated rollbacks per hour for a given customer to avoid flip-flopping.
- Approval-required label for high-impact changes (e.g., quantization profile changes) prevents full rollout without human signoff.
- Safe-apply dry-run mode for all automated recommendations (simulate metrics using traffic shadowing where possible).
state_reconciliation_strategy:
- Source of truth: control-plane desired config stored in audit-backed datastore with versioned config IDs.
- Periodic reconciliation loop (default 60s) fetches desired config for each serving pool, then queries runtime agent endpoints for actual config.
- Diffs produce a three-way merge: desired vs actual vs last-applied to avoid undoing unrelated operator changes.
- Reconciliation is idempotent: operations include a config-version check (CAS) to avoid race conditions, and exponential backoff with jitter on transient failures.
- On detection of partial apply (some nodes updated, some failed), mark impacted nodes as degraded and attempt targeted rollback/apply. If > 30% of nodes are degraded after 10 minutes, escalate to operator.
- Maintain operation history per config ID for forensic and audit purposes.
rollback_playbook:
- Automatic path: rollback initiated by controller when triggers fire for sustained window. Controller issues rollback with reason and target config-version (previous stable).
- Manual path: operator can trigger rollback via Console or API. All manual rollbacks require a short justification message recorded in audit log.
- Post-rollback verification: run a health probe (smoke tests) and verify core metrics return to baseline within 15 minutes. If not, page SRE.
- Re-try policy: controller will attempt one automated re-apply after full rollback only after a cool-down window (default 30 minutes) and only with a changed recommendation or a manual approval.
- Incident escalation: if repeated rollbacks occur for same recommendation, create Investigation ticket and block automated re-applies for that model/workload until triage.
telemetry_and_alerts:
- Required metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, request_rate, error_rate (5xx and model errors), cost_per_request, GPU_utilization, cache_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution.
- Derived signals: rolling baseline (last 24h median), stdev, % change windows, and KS-test p-values for distribution shifts.
- Alerts: PagerDuty page for high-severity rollbacks (customer_impact = high), Slack channel alerts for lower-severity and for canary failures.
- Dashboards: per-customer and per-route rollback timeline with config diffs and before/after metric overlays.
- Audit logs: immutable entries for every automated recommendation, apply, and rollback with actor, timestamp, and diff link.
qa_and_testing_plan:
- Unit tests for trigger evaluation, state diffing, and idempotent apply/rollback logic.
- Emulator tests: run reconciler against a mock runtime that simulates partial failures and slow nodes.
- Canary integration: shadow traffic testing to simulate canary cohorts and verify metric calculation.
- Chaos test: introduce node restarts and network partitions in staging while doing config apply to assert reconciliation handles drift.
- End-to-end pipeline test in CI: run a scenario where a bad recommendation is applied to canary then rolled back automatically, with assertions on audits and alerts.
- Runbook validation: tabletop exercise with SRE and on-call to simulate a rollback incident.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): deploy controller to staging clusters; enable dry-run/simulation mode only. Run end-to-end tests and chaos experiments.
- Phase 2 (canary customers): enable controller real mode for 5% of internal workloads and 1-2 low-risk customers with human override required.
- Phase 3 (gradual expand): increase to 25% cohorts, enable automated rollback for cost/latency triggers but keep quantization/major changes gated by approval.
- Phase 4 (global): enable automated rollbacks for production with full telemetry and runbook validated. Monitor rollback rates and adjust guardrails.
notes:
Design trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive automatic rollbacks reduce customer impact but increase risk of oscillation; mitigated via max-rollback-rate and cool-downs.
- Conservative thresholds reduce false positives but delay mitigation for bad configs. We'll start with conservative thresholds and tighten after observed signal quality improvements.
- Reconciliation frequency is a balance between promptness and control-plane load; default 60s with adaptive backoff.
- Where possible use traffic shadowing for dry-run to avoid exposing customers to untested changes.
